question: Consider the circuit shown consisting of a capacitor $C$, a resistor $R$, an ideal diode $D$, and a square-wave voltage source $V(t)$. The source voltage at the top terminal (with respect to the bottom return line) alternates between $+V_0$ and $-V_0$ with period $T$. The diode is oriented to conduct from the source toward the resistor (left to right in the figure), with zero forward resistance and infinite reverse resistance. Assume each half-cycle is long compared to the time constant, i.e. $\tfrac{T}{2} \gg RC$, and the capacitor is initially uncharged at $t=0$ when $V(t)=+V_0$. Let $Q$ denote the charge on the capacitor plate connected to the resistor $R$. What is the final steady-state value of $Q$ after many cycles?
